issues.reason: "Night fell" predicates no falling — the literal reading is incoherent for a night — so putting the Day/Year terms and Past directly on the event-denoting lantern_night extends the light-verb rule's own rationale (the event-noun's witness IS the eventuality), and every atom emitted is true of the sentence and well-typed; the reviewer's own q2 gap concedes the construction is uncovered.

The standing half is the gap the reviewer also files — Most's third slot is the comparison class and has no room for a restricting domain, so "of the year" goes unrecorded; the widening charge does not stand, since night is exactly the head-noun class the superlative rule puts in that slot and, for a recurring annual night, "of the year" names the comparison cycle rather than carving out a narrower set, so no false or over-asserted atom is emitted.

*Coordination & plurals* states that a bare-plural object in an episodic clause takes an existential group witness when the set takes part in the occurrence, reserving the bare kind filler for non-specific / kind-level objects ("pays tax", "grows wheat"), and "the villagers told stories at the harbor fires until dawn" is a one-off dated occurrence — so (Theme sk_tell_1 story), copied again into the per-member rule, is the storage the instruction set reserves for the other case.

The loss is real — nothing links sk_story_1 to sk_winter_1, so the winter's atoms dangle and the sentence's aboutness is unrecorded — but calling it a parse defect overstates it: an about-of-phrase on a non-derived noun is barred from Possession and given no positive encoding anywhere (the Of oblique is stated only for nominalizations' objects and for position/origin), and every atom the parse did emit is true and well-typed.

gaps_confirmed: Capacity/role "as"-phrase on an event ("lit ... as the speaker of the Council") — no licensed head ties the capacity to the event.
Aboutness "of"-phrase on a non-nominalization noun ("the story of the bad winter") — excluded from Possession, never given a positive encoding.
A time-period subject with an arrival verb ("Lantern-night fell") — the light-verb rule names only occur / happen / take place.
A domain restriction on a superlative ("the longest night of the year") — Most has no slot for the restricting domain.
new_gaps: A named recurring night/period gets one stable name symbol reused for every mention (*Names and casing*), so the type-level claim (Most long lantern_night night) and a single occurrence's atoms ((Past lantern_night), (Time lantern_night (Day 111))) collide on one symbol — nothing licenses separating the recurring named event from that year's instance, and (Past lantern_night) reads as false of the recurring night.

The entity-attached surface-preposition oblique is the obvious carrier for an aboutness of-phrase ((Of sk_story_1 sk_winter_1)), but that open licence is stated only for position/origin prepositions and for nominalizations' objects; extending it explicitly to non-derived nouns would close the "story of the bad winter" gap.
defect_summary: Issue 2: the compliant form mints an existential group witness for the bare-plural object — (GroupOf sk_stories_1 story) with (Theme sk_tell_1 sk_stories_1) on the group event, and a per-binding Skolem group inside the distribution rule ((GroupOf (sk_stories $x) story), (Theme (sk_tell $x) (sk_stories $x))) — the bare kind symbol story being reserved for non-specific / kind-level objects.
notes: The rest of the parse is strong: "that night" resolved by term propagation onto Day 111 / Year 1, the three universals rendered as restriction-in-premise rules with their companions, and the sky-cats' state distributed as per-member Skolem states instead of riding the group symbol. (Manner sk_blow_1 strongly) is manner proper (how the wind blew), not the unslotted degree-adverb class, so it needs no flag.
